overview.historicalContext:
Sophie Germain (1776-1831) was a pioneering French mathematician who made significant contributions to number theory and elasticity theory. Working in an era when women were excluded from formal mathematical education, she corresponded with Gauss and Lagrange under a male pseudonym.

Her work on Fermat's Last Theorem introduced what we now call Sophie Germain primes. She proved that if p is a Sophie Germain prime, then the first case of Fermat's Last Theorem holds for exponent p. This was a major breakthrough, as it provided infinitely many exponents for which FLT was partially verified.

The conjecture that there are infinitely many Sophie Germain primes remains open, analogous to the twin prime conjecture.
overview.problemStatement:
**Definition**: A prime p is a **Sophie Germain prime** if 2p + 1 is also prime.

The prime q = 2p + 1 is called a **safe prime**.

**Examples**: 2, 3, 5, 11, 23, 29, 41, 53, 83, 89, ...

**Structure Theorem**: For p > 3, if p is a Sophie Germain prime, then p ≡ 5 (mod 6).

Equivalently, Sophie Germain primes greater than 3 have the form 6k - 1.
overview.text: A prime p is a Sophie Germain prime if 2p+1 is also prime. We prove that all Sophie Germain primes greater than 3 must have the form 6k-1 (equivalently, p ≡ 5 mod 6).
overview.proofStrategy:
The structure theorem follows from modular arithmetic:

1. **All primes > 3 are ≡ 1 or 5 (mod 6)**: Since primes > 3 are not divisible by 2 or 3, they avoid residue classes 0, 2, 3, 4 (mod 6).

2. **If p ≡ 1 (mod 6)**: Then 2p + 1 ≡ 2·1 + 1 ≡ 3 (mod 6), so 3 | (2p + 1). But 2p + 1 > 3 for p > 1, so 2p + 1 cannot be prime.

3. **Therefore p ≡ 5 (mod 6)**: The only remaining possibility.

This gives the form p = 6k - 1 for some k ≥ 1.
keyInsights: Sophie Germain primes connect directly to Fermat's Last Theorem: Germain proved the first case of FLT holds for exponent p when p is a Sophie Germain prime
The structure theorem eliminates half of potential candidates: primes ≡ 1 (mod 6) are ruled out because 2p+1 ≡ 3 (mod 6) is composite
Safe primes q = 2p + 1 satisfy q ≡ 11 (mod 12) — this further constrains the search space and is important in cryptographic applications
Cunningham chains (cascading Sophie Germain primes via iterated 2p+1) are rare and of interest in computational number theory
The Sophie Germain ↔ safe prime duality is a bijection: every Sophie Germain prime generates exactly one safe prime and vice versa, connecting two important classes in cryptography

sections.title: Verified Examples
sections.summary: Computational verification of 10 Sophie Germain primes: 2, 3, 5, 11, 23, 29, 41, 53, 83, 89.
sections.mathContext: Each $p$ in $\{2, 3, 5, 11, 23, 29, 41, 53, 83, 89\}$ is verified: both $p$ and $2p+1$ are prime, proved by `decide`.

sections.title: Non-Examples
sections.summary: Primes that are NOT Sophie Germain: 7, 13, 17, 19.

sections.title: Structure Theorem
sections.summary: The main result: Sophie Germain primes > 3 must satisfy p ≡ 5 (mod 6). Key lemma: primes > 3 are ≡ 1 or 5 (mod 6), and p ≡ 1 implies 3 | (2p+1).

sections.title: Safe Prime Structure
sections.summary: Properties of safe primes: q ≡ 11 (mod 12) and the Sophie Germain ↔ safe prime equivalence.

sections.title: Cunningham Chain
sections.summary: The chain 2 → 5 → 11 → 23 where each is 2p+1 of the previous.
sections.mathContext: $2 \xrightarrow{2p+1} 5 \xrightarrow{2p+1} 11 \xrightarrow{2p+1} 23 \xrightarrow{2p+1} 47$. Each element is a Sophie Germain prime; $47$ is not ($2 \cdot 47 + 1 = 95$).

crossReferences.description: Sophie Germain's original motivation: she proved the first case of FLT holds for Sophie Germain prime exponents
Whether there are infinitely many Sophie Germain primes remains open, analogous to the infinitude of primes result
The Sophie Germain prime conjecture is analogous to the twin prime conjecture — both ask about structured prime pairs
Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions provides the framework for understanding primes ≡ 5 (mod 6)
Wilson's theorem provides another primality criterion; safe primes have special properties under Wilson's characterization

conclusion.summary:
This formalization provides a complete treatment of Sophie Germain primes, from definition through the main structure theorem. The key result—that Sophie Germain primes greater than 3 must satisfy p ≡ 5 (mod 6)—follows from a clean modular arithmetic argument.

The proof demonstrates how divisibility constraints propagate: if p ≡ 1 (mod 6), then 2p + 1 is divisible by 3, eliminating these candidates. Only p ≡ 5 (mod 6) remains viable.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: **Applications in Cryptography**

Sophie Germain and safe primes are crucial in cryptography:

1. **Diffie-Hellman**: Safe primes ensure the multiplicative group has large prime-order subgroups

**2. RSA**: Some implementations prefer safe primes to resist certain attacks

3. **Pohlig-Hellman**: Safe primes make discrete log harder by avoiding small subgroups

**Connection to Fermat's Last Theorem**

Sophie Germain proved: If p is a Sophie Germain prime, then x^p + y^p = z^p has no solutions with p ∤ xyz (the "first case" of FLT).
openQuestions: Are there infinitely many Sophie Germain primes? (Analogous to twin prime conjecture)
What is the distribution of Sophie Germain primes among all primes?
What is the longest known Cunningham chain of Sophie Germain primes?
